description: A speech the player builds in stages: a short opener, two longer parts at the core on different subjects (the speaker's own stands, work, home, children, school) and a short closer. The player picks one of four at each stage; the pieces are authored to the calibrated rally and council-comment patterns, and every fact is a slot from the speaker's records.

slots.place: The speaker's town, from the household record.
slots.employer: The speaker's employer, from the job record.
slots.years: Years at that employer, computed from the dated tenure record.
slots.school: The speaker's school, from the school record.
slots.number: The count of children in the speaker's household, from the household record.
slots.issue: The subject of a stand, as the bill catalog names its topic.
slots.goal: What the speaker's recorded stand is about, as the bill catalog names the policy; said as a question, then answered.
